answer: One practical anti-sybil mechanism is hardware-backed deposit with per-device liveness checks. Each identity locks a deposit tied to one physical device; the device runs an attested liveness scan, like pressing fingers to a black onyx reader, proving a real person sits behind it. Like shale strata, each new identity must lie on its own device, so an attacker's cost scales linearly: N fake identities demand N deposits plus N real devices in the orchard of their farm, while honest yield per identity stays flat, making mass fakery unprofitable.
